recipes.name: Joe's Fusion Chicken Pad Thai
ingredients_raw: 1 pound boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, cut into bite-size pieces
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (16 ounce) package pad Thai rice noodles

steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Season chicken with salt and black pepper; set aside.
Whisk sugar, cayenne pepper, white wine vinegar, fish sauce, and peanut butter together in a bowl.
Coat the inside of a large skillet or wok with olive oil and place over high heat.
Cook and stir chicken in the hot oil just until the meat is white outside but still pink inside, about 3 minutes.
Remove chicken and set aside in a bowl.
Lower the heat under the skillet to medium-low. Cook and stir garlic in the skillet until it becomes translucent, 1 to 2 minutes.
Cook and stir eggs into garlic until loosely cooked, 2 to 3 minutes.
Pour peanut sauce into the garlic and eggs, and stir to combine. Bring sauce to a simmer.
Stir rice noodles into the boiling water. Cook until noodles are still slightly tough, about 5 minutes.
Return chicken to the skillet with eggs and sauce. Simmer until chicken is no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, stirring frequently, 5 to 8 more minutes.
Stir bean sprouts, rice noodles. and beef broth into the skillet. Bring to a simmer, and cook until noodles are tender and most of the broth has been absorbed, about 10 minutes.
Sprinkle with green onions to serve..

raw_recipe.headline: Joe's Fusion Chicken Pad Thai
raw_recipe.description: This chicken pad Thai's creative ingredients like peanut butter put a spin on the traditional Thai flavors.

review.reviewBody: This had a very nice taste, but was very time consuming.

When I made this as per the recipe my wife thought it had too many noodles. Now I use 11/2 lbs of chicken breast pieces and only 3/4 lb of noodles and 11/2 cups of beef broth. Also, instead of the bean sprouts I add 1 cup of frozen peas and 1 cup of peeled, diced carrots. This makes it much richer tasting, meatier, and more colourful and appetizing. It is a complete meal by itself. Garlic dill pickles make a good accompaniment with it.

This turned out great! Based on other reviews, we reduced the sugar to 1/2 cup and only used about 2/3 of a package of rice noodles. We probably could have reduced the sugar a little bit more. I also added soy sauce to the sauce which I think it needed. We used chicken broth instead of beef broth. We didn't have green onions or cilantro to put on top like traditional pad Thai, but we did top it with crushed peanuts. This was amazing for our first attempt at pad Thai.

Super tasty. But FAR far far too much sugar. I read the reviews before I made this and followed the advice to reduce the sugar to 1/2 cup and fish sauce down to 5 tablespoons. It was STILL far too sweet and salty for me. I'd use 1/4 cup of sugar and 3 tablespoons of fish sauce at first, THEN you can always taste it and add more if you need. It was a bit to 'soupy' for me too, so next time I will only use 1 cup of water in my chicken broth mix.
It has a lovely flavour. I would add the sprouts as you put it on the plate. A little more colour and some peanuts made it perfect

Excellent starting point for pad thai. As many others, I reduced the sugar to 1/2c and only had chicken stock on hand so used that. I also like things on the spicy side so added 1/2 of a minced habanero. This recipe is one that I keep in constant rotation.

This is the best pad thai recipe that I have found. I did make a couple changes based on looking at other pad thai recipes and personal taste. I used rice wine vinegar instead of white wine vinegar because it is what I had in the pantry. I also used a tablespoon of lime juice in place of one of the tablespoons of vinegar and added a little bit of soy sauce to cut the sweetness. I think next time I will use honey or agave in place of half of the sugar. I added quite a bit of red pepper flakes and some sriracha because we like it hot! Otherwise, this is a wonderful recipe....a great basic pad thai recipe that you can amend to your taste.
As we like 'it' hot, I added some sambal. Plus, since I was a bit short on fish sauce, I used tamarind paste. Excellent recipe!!
I cut the sugar to 1/2 cup and used chicken broth instead of beef. This is restaurant quality!

After reading the reviews and to make it a little healthier I only put half the sugar, added a little more cayenne for more spice, more black pepper and added ground ginger to it and it came out perfect.

Really, I'd give this 4.5 stars... almost perfect! I've been searching and searching for a pad thai recipe that tastes like restaurant pad thai. This is the closest I've ever come. I followed the directions exactly just cut the cayenne in half since I have young kids and used rice wine vinegar. I liked the consistency and the flavor was good. I sprinkled lime juice and crushed peanuts on top which I highly recommend. Next time I think I'll put lime juice into the sauce as well. That might be the one flavor missing for me. Oh, and this makes a large amount. I couldn't fit it all in my skillet so when adding everything together at the end, I had to switch to a larger pot. Next time I'll know, and there will definitely be a next time that I make this!

Don't know what I did wrong. It was not appealing when plated. Sesame seed oil overpowered everything. Had to adjust the sauce to compensate. No where near enough peanut butter. It just got lost. Sorry but I won't try this one again.

Very good dish. We enjoyed it and will definitely make it again. A couple changes I would make, add less sugar, only 2 T fish sauce, add more peanut butter and undercook the noodles more. Our noodles were a bit mushy but the sauce had a great flavor and heat.
so much sugar, so little flavor.
The addition of sugar and peanut butter and omission of spices like tanarind paste and chili paste made this more kid friendly and honestly kind of bland, but it isn't bad otherwise

Tasted good but takes longer than the recipe says. I found the noodles were a little too soft for my liking, but that may be because I had to cook it for more than 10 minutes with the broth to thicken it up enough to eat.

This was delicious. Since I didn’t have chicken on hand I used shrimp! Used half the cayenne to accommodate my little ones. Will definitely prepare again! I will try less sugar next time to compare the taste just to try and cut back in calories. Thanks so much!

Holy Smokes....This meal was Great!!!!!! It took me less than 30 minutes to completely prepare, and my wife who is fussy eater loved it....I would defiantly recommend this awesome dish that you can eat Cold or Hot. Great experience...
Excellent flavor, makes a large portion. The family, including my young children love this dish minus the spice.
I did exactly everything the recipe said and it was edible, but my family and I weren't big fans of it. Had a friend over and she liked it, so maybe it was just not a good recipe for my family.
